newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-BOETSCH PREVENTS FRENCH DAVIS CUP WHITEWASH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BOETSCH PREVENTS FRENCH DAVIS CUP WHITEWASH.

text.p: Arnaud Boetsch salvaged a small amount of pride for beaten Davis Cup holders France on Sunday when he defeated Patrick Rafter to prevent a whitewash by Australia in their world group first round tie.
Boetsch downed Rafter 4-6 6-4 7-6 (7-5) in the final singles match after Australia had wrapped up the tie by taking an unassailable 3-0 lead by winning Saturday's doubles.

Sandon Stolle gave Australia the chance of a 5-0 victory when he defeated French number one Cedric Pioline 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 in the first of the reverse singles on Sunday. The reverse singles were decided by the best of three sets instead of five because the results did not influence the outcome of the tie.

In taking the second set against Rafter, Boetsch ended a run of 12 consecutive sets won by the Australians, starting with Rafter's tenacious fightback against Pioline in the opening singles match on Friday.

Rafter dropped the first two sets against Pioline before winning the next three, with Mark Woodforde beating Boetsch in straight sets in the second singles match. Woodforde then combined with long-time partner Todd Woodbridge to beat Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux in three sets in Saturday's doubles.
Stolle was called up by Australia captain John Newcombe early on Sunday to replace Woodforde when the left-hander complained of an arm injury after a busy schedule over the previous two days.
Stolle took full advantage of his call-up to win his first Davis Cup singles match for Australia.
Boetsch's win over Rafter came as small consolation for France, who just nine weeks ago had celebrated a dramatic 3-2 Davis Cup final win over Sweden in Malmo.
